objective: Targeted manual review of legacy mock Chemistry tests and definitions after v176 Mechanics, with both correct and incorrect input checks

corrections.previousFront: What does Tollens' reagent do with an aldehyde?
corrections.previousBack: It is reduced to silver, producing a silver mirror; ketones give no reaction.
corrections.newFront: What visible result does an aldehyde give with Tollens' reagent?
corrections.newBack: A silver mirror or grey silver deposit.
corrections.reason: Single directly assessable observation, instead of requiring an unrelated ketone comparison.

corrections.previousFront: How does Group 2 reactivity change down the group?
corrections.previousBack: It increases because outer electrons are further from the nucleus and more shielded, so ionisation energies fall.
corrections.newFront: How does Group 2 metal reactivity change down the group?
corrections.reason: One trend per card; explanations remain on other cards and in exam practice.

marking.legacyFailure: Wrong chloride/iodide colour pairing was given full credit by unordered keyword concepts.
marking.fix: Evaluate three explicit ion–precipitate-colour pairs; accept reversed presentation order and ion formulae, give partial for two correct, reject swapped colours.
marking.tollensLegacyFailure: The generic phrase matcher fully credited negated silver-mirror results or wrongly assigned silver mirrors to ketones.
marking.tollensFix: Explicit result semantics accept normal silver-mirror wording while rejecting negation and incorrect ketone attribution.
